text:
Marisol (Marketing Lead): quick sync - we need a lightweight battlecard update for the launch next week: focus on 1) claims that land with platform eng + procurement, 2) 2 hero lines to A/B on the webinar signup, 3) routing for inbound demos. who can help?
Evan (Growth): I can take hero-line tests. want 2 very different approaches: technical-cred vs business-saver.
Priya (Field): i'll do the field-facing boil-down: 3 bullets + 4 quick rebuttals. keep it scannable for SDRs.
Tom (Bench): sharing fresh numbers now. note: public bench runs vary a lot by seq len. suggest we avoid absolute p95 claims; instead "stable tail under load with multi-tier fallback". link: https://redwood-internal/bench/1767 (uploaded)
Nadia (Product): add a short line about deployment modes: "deploy same runtime in-hosted, dedicated, or your VPC". also call out enterprise SLAs / reserved pools.
Marisol (Marketing Lead): good. Priya - can you make 2 versions of the battlecard: (A) procurement-first (cost + reserved contracts) (B) reliability-first (SLA + fallback routing). under each include 3 soundbites and 3 rebuttals. keep each card <200 words.
Priya (Field): on it. examples for rebuttals:
  - competitor: "we have more GPU capacity" -> reply: "capacity isn't the same as per-request predictability; we route and degrade gracefully to keep UX consistent"
  - competitor: "your platform is more complex" -> reply: "one API surface for hosted/dedicated/private, plus onboarding playbook & POC templates"
  - procurement: "we need cost guarantees" -> reply: "reserved capacity + transparent per-token breakdown in the console"
Evan (Growth): hero lines idea:
  - Tech angle: "Predictable inference. No surprises at scale."
  - Biz angle: "Cut inference spend and protect your SLAs."
Tom (Bench): small caution: from run 1767, model-X p50 is great on short seqs; p95 shows variance with cold starts. recommend the battlecard proof be a relative stat: "consistent low p50 on typical queries; automatic cache & warmup reduce cold-starts".
Nadia (Product): also add a short demo script for the webinar: 10m live failover (route to secondary region), 6m cost dashboard walkthrough, 4m Q&A. callout: show "route policy change -> <60s to take effect" as an ops flex.
Marisol (Marketing Lead): solid. Ops routing for inbound: use utm_campaign=llm-launch-2026, add tag=procurement or tag=reliability depending on signup answers. growth handles procurement, AE team handles reliability. Evan will wire flows in Hubspot.
Evan (Growth): i'll set up forms with a short qualifying checkbox: "priority: lower cost / predictable latency" -> maps to tag. will also create two landing headlines to A/B.
Priya (Field): final ask: include 1 tiny visual showing "fallback chain" and 1 line on security (KMS + private control plane). i'll draft the two battlecards and post for review by 5pm PT.
Tom (Bench): i'll provide 1-sentence bench blurbs suitable for the card: short, conservative phrasing only. posting now.
ops-bot: inbound workflow created: campaign=llm-launch-2026, endpoint=/forms/llm-launch, tags=[procurement,reliability].
Marisol (Marketing Lead): deadlines: Priya = B-cards by 5pm, Evan = landing A/B by EOD, Tom = bench blurbs by 3pm, Nadia = slides + demo script by tomorrow 9am. quick review at 4:30 if anyone can join. thanks!
Evan (Growth): joining 4:30. will bring suggested microscopy for CTAs.
Nadia (Product): adding demo notes to the slide deck and will flag any prod caveats.
Priya (Field): drafting now. :sparkles:
Tom (Bench): posted conservative wording: "bench run 1767 shows durable p50 on short queries; multi-tier caching reduces cold-start variance"
Marisol (Marketing Lead): great work team. let's keep the language tested and conservative on numbers. we'll iterate based on internal playbook feedback after the review.
